text:
sam: Quick update — ran the kv-slab + continuous-batcher tuning on canary nodes (rack-a, rack-b). Wanted to share profiling snippets and propose a small soft-429 rollout.

sam: TL;DR: reducing token_budget target from 1600 -> 1100 reduced 95p latency by ~12% under mixed short/long workloads, KV hit ratio unchanged (~72%). However saw slightly more micro-429s during bursty tail (spike windows).

jess: nice. can you paste the perf numbers/command you ran?

sam: pasted results below (raw):
```
# run: ./tools/bench --scenario=mixed --duration=15m --batcher=continuous --kv-profile=slab
requests: 180k
mean_latency_ms: 82
p95_latency_ms: 218 -> 192 (after token_budget=1100)
kv_hit_rate: 0.72
soft_429_count: 38 (before: 12)
cpu_gpu_util: 68/74
```

arjun: fwiw, that soft_429 jump worries me. did you correlate with kernel choice? maybe smaller batches forced the wavkernel -> small-kernel path more often?

sam: good call. i profiled kernel selection traces: more smaller-batch kernel invocations (+18% small-kernel), and those have slightly higher per-token overhead. attached snippet from profiler bot below.

ci-bot: profiler: kernel_switch_events: { small_kernel: 11234, wav_kernel: 5031, fused_kernel: 412 }
ci-bot: avg_batch_size_before: 5.3 -> after: 3.9

maria: could be the continuous-batcher batch-formation threshold being too aggressive on latency-first routes. maybe we should add a soft min_batch_time or prefer kv-hit coalescing?

jess: +1. what if we bias batch formation: prefer waiting up to 8ms when kv-cache hit ratio >= 0.7 and request token length < 200, otherwise keep current fast-path? that would nudge avg_batch up a bit.

arjun: also consider increasing token_budget only for routes with high kv locality. token_budget is global currently right?

sam: yes global now. i prototyped a route-aware token_budget flag: per-route overrides via routing key. small config sample:
```json
{"flow_control": {"default_token_budget": 1100, "overrides": {"/chat/short": 1400, "/embed/*": 800}}}
```

maria: love the route-aware idea. ops-bot — any SLO concerns if we start route overrides?

ops-bot: quick check: current alerting thresholds: soft_429_rate > 0.05 over 5m triggers pager. Canary saw 38 soft_429s over 15m (~0.0002 rate) — below pager but worth tracking.

jess: proposal: revert token_budget to 1400 global for now, but enable route overrides for the short-chat route with 1800, and deploy batcher tweak to wait up to 8ms when kv_hit >= 0.7. rollout plan: 5% -> 25% -> 50% canary over 3 hours if error/latency stable.

arjun: add a kernel-sampler flag too: prefer fused_kernel for batches where avg_len > 600 to avoid extra small-kernel churn. we can gate that behind feature flag.

sam: ack. i'll open a small PR (will tag here) with: 1) per-route token_budget, 2) batcher wait bias when kv_hit high, 3) kernel preference sampler heuristic.

sam: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1893 (draft). please review.

jess: nit: add a metric for "batching_delay_ms" so we can see if the 8ms wait actually increases client-observed latency for short single-turn requests.

ci-bot: perf_pump: ran quick canary with routes overrides enabled (5%): p95 reduced from 210 -> 185 on short-chat. overall soft_429s increased from 12 -> 16.

maria: those look promising. action items: sam to add metrics + PR tests, jess to add rollout plan in runbook, arjun to add kernel sampling unit test, ops to monitor soft_429 dashboard.

sam: plan to ship draft PR to canary tonight at 22:00 UTC. will post canary-run command and config when kicking off.

jess: thanks — also create a quick smoke script: `./smoke_check --route=/chat/short --qps=80 --dur=2m` and post results to #eng-runtime-canary.

arjun: one more thought — for the soft-429 policy we should distinguish "micro-429s" (ephemeral + recoverable) vs sustained; maybe only escalate sustained >3min. ops-bot can we add that to alerting?

ops-bot: noted. will change alert to require >3m sustained rate for paging. will post PR to ops-alerts repo.

sam: thanks all. i'll update the thread with canary metrics after deploy. :thumbsup:
